desk.headline: Group HEPS up 8.4% to 39.8p; Investec Limited interim dividend 417c (from 396c); ROE target kept
results: Adjusted operating profit rose 5.6% to £494.5m, but only about 0.3% at constant currency; a stronger rand lifted the sterling figures.
Adjusted EPS rose 7.4% to 43.5p, just above the 41.7–43.3p range flagged in September; HEPS rose 8.4% to 39.8p from 36.7p.
Revenue grew 6.7% to £1.17bn while operating costs rose 9.7% to £623.8m, lifting the cost-to-income ratio to 53.3% from 51.9%; ROE was 13.5%.
Southern Africa profit rose 13.6% to £270.6m; UK and other fell 2.7% to £223.9m. The credit loss ratio improved to 28bp from 35bp.
Investec Limited shareholders get a gross interim dividend of 417c (396c a year ago); the group payout is 42.5%, within the 35–50% policy.

guidance.summary: Investec kept its full-year targets: group ROE of 13–14% and a cost-to-income ratio of 52–54%. It slightly adjusted its UK return target to a 12–13% ROTE; the earlier UK figure was not stated in the coverage read.

points: CEO Fani Titi described a steady improvement in underlying performance; SA private clients grew 7.9% annualised to about 132,000.
The CFO said costs are rising faster than revenue because of investment in new platforms; this year should be the peak, with payback from FY2028.
Lower average interest rates (about 20bp lower in SA, 45bp in the UK) weighed on interest income; the UK team expects rates to drift up.
Management called loan-book quality strong but warned of tough markets and fierce competition for good lending deals.
Rathbones cost savings reached £76m a year, ahead of the roughly £60m expected when the deal was signed.
call.source: Results call transcript — Investing.com, 19 Nov 2026; Business Explainer, 19 Nov 2026; AskTraders, 19 Nov 2026

watch: Whether cost growth slows as the investment programme peaks this year.
UK specialist bank profits and returns against the 12–13% ROTE target.
Rand moves, which flatter or hurt the sterling results, and regulatory approval of the planned Shoprite banking partnership.
